parsed.explanation: Traveller-facing evidence is mixed. Positives: gender identity has been covered by hate-crime law since 2018 and by hate-speech law since 2019, trans status was depathologised in 2017, the 2025 gender-recognition reform is resident-facing, and a visitor-facing hostile statute is absent. Negatives: a company-wide pool-chain rule denies trans customers their chosen changing rooms (contested, but a known everyday exposure that reaches public facilities), and scholars document political intimidation of trans advocates, though this is not state targeting of visitors. Visitor-specific data on violence, border checks, police practice and detention placement is absent, and the hate-crime dataset records only police-identified motives, so it shows little about prevalence. I weigh the documented facility restriction and political climate as a step below the acceptance-with-protections tier, and the operating hate-crime recourse as a real offset. The sexuality-law items are tangential.
